segments.text: I'm here with Scott Kaiser, who is the president of Laser Maintenance Group, in terms of routine
laser maintenance. How often would you recommend doing that? The OEM asks for a thousand hour
maintenance. Some people are running two shifts, some people are running three, some people run
one. A thousand hours would be every six months. These guys run two shifts a day, but they leave
their laser on two 10-hour shifts, so they run 20 hours out of 24 hours. So they hit their
maintenance interval every six weeks. Okay. But it's just the machine's still running,
we hate to slow down to stop for that. Well, now you just lost, it's not so much the cost of this.
This was, you know, relatively inexpensive as far as parts go. It could have been catastrophic,
but it's also the time, the two, you know, two days a time that it took to
get in there and then a few hours to fix it and then bring the machine back up.
